List grammars — on real screens

The fitting room shows the three grammars on three demo rows, which is enough to understand them and not enough to choose. These are the live screens, lifted out of the prototypes by the generator — left is exactly what ships today, right is the same markup with the other grammar applied as CSS. Nothing here is decided.

Settings — a fixed handful of identical menu rows

Seven rows that are all the same shape, and the screen is nothing else. Today each one separates itself from the page — seven edges to get right in light. As a container it separates once and the hairlines do the rest. flows/coach/settings.html #s-settings

Messages — hundreds of identical records

This screen ALREADY uses the third grammar — nobody wrote it down, it was simply drawn that way. Which is the finding: we own all three and choose between them by accident. The only thing missing is the hairline, so rows currently run together. flows/shared/messages.html #s-messages

Personal data — a form

The case that started the whole thread. Today: nine separate fields, each needing its own fill and edge on a near-white page. As a container the fields need neither — which is exactly why iOS has no outlined text field. flows/coach/personal-data.html #s-personal-data
